items.claim: Sourcing before compinit errors at startup and never registers completion
items.consequence: A user who follows the new FAQ instruction but whose `.zshrc` has not run `compinit` before the `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` line (or never runs it, as in a stock zsh setup) gets `_rg:341: command not found: _arguments` on every shell start, and `rg <TAB>` never completes rg options in that session, even if `compinit` runs later. The guard treats 'compdef is not defined' as 'run the completion function now', which is only right for ci/test-complete; for a real user it is the same kind of confusing failure the PR set out to remove, and the FAQ does not state the ordering requirement. Sourcing after `compinit` works as the PR intends.
items.proposed_fix: Minimum: say in the FAQ's sourcing paragraph that the `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` line must come after `compinit` has run in `.zshrc` (and, for the recommended method, that the `fpath=` line must come before `compinit`). Optionally also make the failure self-explanatory by deciding 'run the completion now' from completion context rather than from `compdef` being absent, replacing rg.zsh:441-445 with: `if (( $+compstate )) || [[ $_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS == (1|t*|y*) ]]; then _rg "$@"; elif (( ! $+functions[compdef] )); then print -ru2 -- "rg: zsh completions must be sourced after compinit has run"; else compdef _rg rg; fi`. Checked in scratch on zsh 5.8.1 only: that guard kept fpath autoload, source-after-compinit and the ci/test-complete list mode (341 specs, with or without compdef defined) working and turned source-before-compinit into the clear message. Assumption not checked: `$+compstate` behaves the same on the pre-5.4 zsh versions the script still supports.

FAQ.md:131-136 -- 'Or if you'd prefer to load and generate completions at the same time, you can add the following to your `$HOME/.zshrc` file:' followed by the source line, with no mention of compinit ordering

Observed (zsh 5.8.1, interactive session driven through a pty, packaged _rg removed from fpath, template with !ENCODINGS! filled by hand): source then compinit printed `_rg:341: command not found: _arguments`; `rg --generate=complete-zs<TAB>` left the word uncompleted twice and `_comps[rg]` stayed unset.
Observed (same setup): compinit then source completed `--generate=complete-zs` to `complete-zsh` on both attempts, so the documented happy path works.
Observed (same setup): adding the fpath entry after compinit left `_comps[rg]` unset and nothing completed, the mirror-image ordering requirement of the recommended method.

items.claim: Guard keys on the literal name _rg and misfires under other names
items.consequence: The guard recognises the autoload case only when the running function is literally named `_rg`, and that test is wrong in both directions. If the script is on fpath under another name (it carries `#compdef rg`, so compinit binds it whatever the file is called), the first `rg <TAB>` in each new shell completes nothing and only the second works; before this change that install completed on the first TAB. Conversely `cd ~/.zsh-complete && source _rg` makes `$funcstack[1]` equal `_rg`, so the script still calls `_rg` outside completion and prints the exact error from the linked issue.
items.proposed_fix: Decide 'run the completion now' by completion context instead of by name, using the same replacement guard as finding 1: `if (( $+compstate )) || [[ $_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS == (1|t*|y*) ]]; then _rg "$@"; elif (( ! $+functions[compdef] )); then print -ru2 -- "rg: zsh completions must be sourced after compinit has run"; else compdef _rg rg; fi`. In scratch on zsh 5.8.1 this completed on the first and second TAB for a file installed as `_ripgrep`, and `cd <dir> && source _rg` registered cleanly instead of erroring. Narrow case: every installer in the repo (FAQ, ci/build-and-publish-m2, the Homebrew formula) writes the file as `_rg`, so leaving it is defensible.

items.claim: FAQ .zshrc snippet includes a shell prompt and fails verbatim
items.consequence: The FAQ says to add the following line to `$HOME/.zshrc` and then shows it with a leading `$ ` prompt. Pasted as written, zsh reports `command not found: $` at startup and the completions are never loaded. The `fpath=(...)` snippet a few lines above, also meant for `.zshrc`, has no prompt; dropping it here makes the two file snippets consistent and copy-pasteable.
items.proposed_fix: Change FAQ.md:135 from `$ source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` to `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)`, matching the prompt-less `fpath=($HOME/.zsh-complete $fpath)` snippet at FAQ.md:128. While in that paragraph, FAQ.md:138 is missing its subject: 'easier to setup, is generally slower' reads better as 'easier to set up, it is generally slower'.

native_payload.intent: Make ripgrep's generated zsh completion script usable by sourcing it directly (`source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)`) as well as by installing it as `_rg` on fpath: call `_rg` only when autoloaded as `_rg` or when `compdef` is undefined, otherwise register with `compdef _rg rg`. Must not regress fpath autoload or ci/test-complete; FAQ.md documents both zsh methods and fixes a typo.

residual_risks: ci/test-complete now depends on `compdef` being undefined in the zsh that runs it: with the completion system loaded, `( _RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS=1 source rg.zsh )` printed 0 specs in scratch (341 without it), which would hit the script's 'Failed to get comp_args' exit. That needs a zshenv that loads compinit for non-interactive shells; nothing in the repo's CI suggests one. (adversarial; reproduced in this review)

All behaviour was observed on zsh 5.8.1 only, against the template with the !ENCODINGS! placeholder filled in by hand; real `rg --generate complete-zsh` output, cargo build/test and ci/test-complete were unavailable in this environment. The script still carries a compatibility path for zsh older than 5.4, and the new guard's `$funcstack` / `$+functions[compdef]` behaviour there was not checked.
ksh_autoload-style loading of the fpath file was not exercised; compinit autoloads with -z, so this is outside the normal path. (adversarial)
testing_gaps: No in-repo test exercises either real-use branch of the new guard: ci/test-complete only sources the file with _RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS=1 and no completion system, reaching `_rg "$@"` through the compdef-undefined arm. The `compdef _rg rg` arm (source after compinit) and the `$funcstack[1] == _rg` arm (fpath autoload) are untested, so a regression in either install method would not fail CI.
